name: Garden Sage
imageAlt: Illustration of garden sage with soft grey-green leaves
description: A hardy perennial with soft, silvery-green leaves and a warm, peppery, slightly piney flavor. Sage has been grown in kitchens and medicine gardens for centuries and its purple flowers are loved by bees.

growingConditions.watering: Moderate; let the soil dry out between waterings
growingConditions.soilType: Light, well-draining, neutral to slightly alkaline soil

uses: Fried in brown butter for pasta and gnocchi
Dried leaf tea and herbal gargles
Sage tea or a cooled infusion is a traditional gargle for sore throats and mouth irritation
Traditionally taken to ease mild indigestion and bloating
Folk remedy for excessive sweating and hot flashes
benefits: Contains rosmarinic acid and other antioxidants
Has natural antibacterial properties that help preserve food and freshen breath
Some small studies suggest sage extract may support memory and alertness
medicinal.caution: Common sage contains thujone, so enjoy it in cooking and tea amounts only. Avoid medicinal doses and the essential oil during pregnancy or if you have epilepsy.
